title: Building an Argument
description: Link ideas clearly to write a balanced argumentative essay: contrast (although, despite, whereas, however), purpose (so that, in order to, so as to), result (so...that, such...that, therefore, as a result), and addition and sequencing linkers. Vocabulary: social issues and debate language.
objectives: Express contrast with although, even though, whereas, despite and however
Express purpose with in order to, so as to and so that
Express result with so...that, such...that, therefore and as a result
Organise a balanced argumentative essay with addition and sequencing linkers

lessons.title: Contrast: Although, Even Though, Whereas
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan kontras dengan although, though, even though, whereas, dan while.
objectives: Use although, though and even though + clause
Use whereas and while to compare two different facts
Avoid using although and but in the same sentence
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Conjunctions of contrast + clause
These words are **conjunctions**: they are followed by a full clause (subject + verb).

| Linker | Meaning / use | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| although | neutral contrast | **Although** it was raining, we went for a walk. |
| though | more informal; can go at the end | It was raining. We went for a walk, **though**. |
| even though | stronger, more surprising contrast | **Even though** she was exhausted, she finished the report. |
| whereas / while | compares two different facts | My brother loves cities, **whereas** I prefer villages. |

### Position and punctuation
- The clause can come first or second: *Although it was late, we kept working.* / *We kept working although it was late.*
- Use a comma when the *although*-clause comes first.
- *Though* at the end of a sentence acts like *however*: *The food was great. The service was slow, **though**.*

### Don't double up!
In English, **although** and **but** cannot be used together:
- ✗ *Although he trained every day, but he didn't win.*
- ✓ *Although he trained every day, he didn't win.*
- ✓ *He trained every day, but he didn't win.*

### whereas vs although
*Whereas* and *while* compare two facts that are **different but not surprising**; *although* introduces a fact that makes the main clause **surprising**:
- *Rina is outgoing, **whereas** her sister is shy.* (simple difference)
- ***Although** Rina is shy, she loves acting.* (surprising)

### even though vs even if
- *even though* = despite the fact that (it **is** true): *Even though I'm tired, I'll come.*
- *even if* = whether or not (it **might** be true): *Even if I'm tired, I'll come.*

> **Catatan:** Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering berkata *Meskipun ..., tetapi ...*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **jangan** memakai *although* dan *but* sekaligus. Pilih salah satu. *Whereas* ≈ *sedangkan*.

examples.en: Although it was raining, we went for a walk along the river.

examples.id: Hotelnya bagus. Tapi agak jauh dari pantai.

vocabulary.example: Some people save, whereas others spend everything.
In contrast, rural areas are quieter.
She's outgoing, whereas her sister is shy.
It's surprising that he won, although he trained hard.
It was difficult; nonetheless, we succeeded.

grammar.pattern: Although / Even though + clause, + main clause
grammar.example: Although the test was hard, I passed.
I like tea, whereas my wife prefers coffee.
It's expensive. It's worth it, though.

mistakes.wrong: Although he trained every day, but he didn't win.
mistakes.right: Although he trained every day, he didn't win.
mistakes.why: Don't use although and but in the same sentence.

mistakes.wrong: Although the rain, we played outside.
mistakes.right: Although it was raining, we played outside.
mistakes.why: Although needs a full clause (subject + verb), not just a noun.

mistakes.wrong: Even though, he passed the exam.
mistakes.right: Even so, he passed the exam.
mistakes.why: Even though is a conjunction and needs a clause; to start a sentence use Even so or However.

sections.summary: **Although, though, even though** + clause show contrast (*even though* is stronger). **Whereas/while** compare two different facts. Never combine *although* with *but*, and remember that these words need a full clause. *Ringkasan: meskipun = although (tanpa but); sedangkan = whereas.*

reviewCards.back: Use either although or but, not both.

questions.instructions: Hint: the gap is followed by a full clause (subject + verb).
questions.text: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk along the river.
questions.explanation: **Although + clause** (*it was raining*). *Despite* needs a noun or -ing form, and *However* joins two separate sentences.

questions.sentence: The flat is small. It's very comfortable.
answers: Although the flat is small, it's very comfortable.
Although the flat is small, it is very comfortable.
questions.explanation: **Although + clause, + main clause**: *Although the flat is small, it's very comfortable.*

options: My brother loves crowded cities, whereas I prefer quiet villages.
Whereas it was late, we kept working.
I was tired, whereas I finished my homework.
Whereas the rain, the match continued.
questions.explanation: **Whereas** compares two different facts about two people or things. It doesn't express a surprising contrast like *although*.
Don't use *although* and *but* together: **Although he trained every day, he didn't win the race.**

questions.text: I really enjoyed the film. It was a bit too long, ___.
answers: though
questions.explanation: **Though** at the end of a sentence is an informal way to say *however*.

options: Even though she was exhausted, she finished the report.
Though the traffic was bad, we arrived on time.
Although of the cost, they bought the house.
While some people prefer tea, others can't live without coffee.
Even though, he passed the exam.
questions.explanation: *Even though / though / while* + clause are correct. *Although of* is wrong (use *despite the cost*), and *even though* cannot stand alone at the start of a sentence.

lessons.title: Contrast: Despite, In Spite Of, However
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan kontras dengan despite/in spite of (+ kata benda/-ing) dan however/nevertheless (antar kalimat).
objectives: Use despite and in spite of + noun, -ing or the fact that
Use however, nevertheless and on the other hand to link sentences
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### despite / in spite of: prepositions
*Despite* and *in spite of* have the same meaning as *although*, but they are **prepositions**, so they are followed by a **noun, pronoun or -ing form**, not a clause.

| Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- |
| despite / in spite of + noun | **Despite the rain**, we enjoyed the trip. |
| despite / in spite of + -ing | **In spite of feeling** ill, she went to work. |
| despite / in spite of + the fact that + clause | **Despite the fact that** it was raining, we went out. |

⚠️ Common errors:
- ✗ *despite of* → ✓ *despite* or *in spite of*
- ✗ *despite it was raining* → ✓ *despite the rain / although it was raining*

### Transforming although → despite
| Although | Despite |
| --- | --- |
| Although she was ill, ... | Despite **being ill** / Despite **her illness**, ... |
| Although the traffic was heavy, ... | Despite **the heavy traffic**, ... |
| Although he is rich, ... | Despite **being rich** / Despite **his wealth**, ... |

### Sentence linkers: however, nevertheless, on the other hand
These words connect **two sentences**. They are usually followed by a comma and often begin a new sentence (or follow a semicolon).

| Linker | Style | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| However, | neutral | The hotel was expensive. **However**, it was very clean. |
| Nevertheless, / Nonetheless, | formal; 'in spite of this' | The risks are high. **Nevertheless**, we will continue. |
| On the other hand, | presents the other side | Cities offer jobs. **On the other hand**, they are expensive. |
| Even so, | informal/neutral | It was cold. **Even so**, we swam. |

### Punctuation
- ✓ *The plan was risky. However, it worked.*
- ✓ *The plan was risky; however, it worked.*
- ✗ *The plan was risky, however it worked.* (comma splice)

### Choosing the right word
| You want to contrast... | Use |
| --- | --- |
| two clauses in one sentence | although / even though / whereas |
| a noun/-ing with a clause | despite / in spite of |
| two sentences | however / nevertheless / on the other hand |

> **Catatan:** *Despite* dan *in spite of* = *meskipun / walaupun*, tetapi diikuti **kata benda atau -ing**, bukan kalimat. Jangan pernah menulis *despite of*. *However* = *namun*, biasanya di awal kalimat baru diikuti koma.

vocabulary.example: Despite his age, he runs every day.
It was hard. Nevertheless, we finished.
The match went ahead despite the rain.
The trip was expensive but worth it.
Despite a lack of funding, the project succeeded.

grammar.pattern: Despite / In spite of + noun / -ing, + clause
Despite the fact that + clause, + clause
grammar.example: Despite the fact that he worked hard, he failed.
grammar.note: Use the fact that to add a clause.

mistakes.wrong: Despite of the delays, the project was finished on time.
mistakes.right: Despite the delays, the project was finished on time.
mistakes.why: Use despite or in spite of, never despite of.

mistakes.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
mistakes.right: Despite the rain, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite is a preposition and cannot be followed by a clause.

mistakes.wrong: The plan was risky, however it worked.
mistakes.right: The plan was risky. However, it worked.
mistakes.why: However links two sentences; use a full stop or semicolon before it and a comma after it.

sections.summary: **Despite / in spite of** + noun, -ing or *the fact that* + clause; never *despite of*. **However, nevertheless, on the other hand, even so** link two sentences and need correct punctuation. *Ringkasan: although + kalimat; despite + kata benda/-ing; however + kalimat baru.*

reviewCards.back: noun, -ing, or the fact that + clause
Despite being ill / Despite her illness

questions.text: We really enjoyed the trip in spite ___ the rain.
answers: of
questions.explanation: The full form is **in spite of** + noun.

questions.sentence: Although she was ill, she went to work.
answers: Despite being ill, she went to work.
Despite her illness, she went to work.
Despite the fact that she was ill, she went to work.
questions.explanation: *Despite* + -ing / noun / *the fact that*: **Despite being ill, she went to work.**

questions.prompt: Complete the review with words from the bank.

answers: Despite
However
Although
questions.explanation: **Despite** + noun (*the high price*); **However,** + new sentence; **Although** + clause (*it rained all evening*). *Despite of* doesn't exist.
Use **Despite** or **In spite of**, never *despite of*.

questions.text: The hotel was very expensive. ___, it was worth every penny.
questions.explanation: A linker between two sentences, followed by a comma → **Nevertheless** (= however). *Despite* and *although* cannot be used like this.

questions.source: Meskipun cuacanya buruk, penerbangan kami tidak tertunda.
answers: Despite the bad weather, our flight wasn't delayed.
Despite the bad weather, our flight was not delayed.
In spite of the bad weather, our flight wasn't delayed.
In spite of the bad weather, our flight was not delayed.
Although the weather was bad, our flight wasn't delayed.
Although the weather was bad, our flight was not delayed.
Even though the weather was bad, our flight wasn't delayed.
Even though the weather was bad, our flight was not delayed.
Though the weather was bad, our flight wasn't delayed.
Despite the terrible weather, our flight wasn't delayed.
questions.explanation: Use **Despite/In spite of + noun** (*the bad weather*) or **Although + clause** (*the weather was bad*).

lessons.title: Purpose: In Order To, So As To, So That
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan tujuan dengan to, in order to, so as to, so that, dan bentuk negatifnya.
objectives: Use to, in order to and so as to + infinitive
Use so that + can/could/will/would for purpose with a different subject
Form negative purpose with so as not to, in order not to and so that ... won't
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Purpose with an infinitive
| Linker | Style | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| to + verb | neutral, most common | I'm saving money **to buy** a car. |
| in order to + verb | more formal / emphatic | The council cut costs **in order to reduce** debt. |
| so as to + verb | formal | We left early **so as to avoid** the traffic. |

### Negative purpose
Don't say *not to* alone for purpose; use:
- ***so as not to** + verb*: *I whispered **so as not to wake** the baby.*
- ***in order not to** + verb*: *He took notes **in order not to forget** anything.*
- ✗ *I left early for not missing the bus.*

### so that + clause
Use **so that** when the purpose clause has a **different subject** or needs a **modal**:
| Time | Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| present/future | so that + can / will | I'll send the map **so that you can find** us. |
| past | so that + could / would | She spoke slowly **so that everyone could understand**. |
| negative | so that + won't / wouldn't | We whispered **so that we wouldn't wake** the baby. |

In informal speech, *that* is often dropped: *I'll send the map **so** you can find us.*

### for + noun
Use **for + noun** to express purpose with a thing: *I went to the pharmacy **for some medicine**.* But NOT *for + verb*: ✗ *I went there for buy medicine.* / ✗ *for buying medicine* (when talking about a person's purpose).

### in case is not purpose
*Take a jacket **in case** it gets cold* = as a precaution (from Unit 3). Compare: *Take a jacket **so that** you don't get cold.*

### In essays
Purpose linkers are useful for explaining policies: *The government should invest in public transport **so that** fewer people drive, **in order to** reduce pollution.*

> **Catatan:** *untuk / agar / supaya* dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa diterjemahkan menjadi **to / in order to** (subjek sama) atau **so that** (subjek berbeda atau butuh modal). Jangan menulis *for + kata kerja* untuk tujuan: *untuk membeli* = **to buy**, bukan *for buy*.

examples.en: I'm saving money in order to buy a car.
examples.id: Saya menabung untuk membeli mobil.

examples.en: She spoke slowly so that everyone could understand her.
examples.id: Dia berbicara pelan agar semua orang bisa memahaminya.

examples.en: We left early so as not to get stuck in traffic.
examples.id: Kami berangkat lebih awal supaya tidak terjebak macet.

examples.en: I went to the pharmacy for some medicine.
examples.id: Saya pergi ke apotek untuk membeli obat.

vocabulary.example: What is the purpose of your visit?
We left early so as to avoid the crowds.
They whispered so as not to wake the baby.
I set two alarms so that I wouldn't oversleep.

grammar.pattern: main clause + (in order / so as) to + verb
grammar.example: He moved to Seoul to study Korean.

grammar.pattern: main clause + so as not to / in order not to + verb
grammar.example: I wrote it down so as not to forget.

grammar.pattern: main clause + so that + subject + can/could/will/would
grammar.example: I'll leave the light on so that you can see.

mistakes.wrong: She took a taxi for not being late.
mistakes.right: She took a taxi so as not to be late.
mistakes.why: Negative purpose uses so as not to / in order not to + verb.

mistakes.wrong: I went to the bank for open an account.
mistakes.right: I went to the bank to open an account.
mistakes.why: Purpose with a verb uses to + infinitive, not for.

mistakes.wrong: I study hard so that pass the exam.
mistakes.right: I study hard so that I can pass the exam.
mistakes.why: So that is followed by a full clause with a subject (and usually a modal).

sections.summary: Express purpose with **to / in order to / so as to + verb** (same subject) and **so that + subject + can/could/will/would** (different subject or modal). For negatives, use **so as not to / in order not to** or **so that ... won't/wouldn't**. Use *for* only with nouns. *Ringkasan: untuk + kata kerja = to + V1, bukan for + V1.*

reviewCards.front: in order to / so as to + verb

reviewCards.back: for some medicine / to buy medicine

questions.instructions: Hint: the gap is followed by a verb (buy).
questions.text: I'm saving money ___ buy a car.
questions.explanation: Purpose + base verb → **in order to buy**. *So that* needs a subject; *for* cannot be followed by a verb.

questions.prompt: Join the sentences using so that.
questions.sentence: She spoke slowly. She wanted everyone to understand her.
questions.cue: Begin with: She spoke slowly so that ...
answers: She spoke slowly so that everyone could understand her.
She spoke slowly so that everyone would understand her.
She spoke slowly so that everyone understood her.
She spoke slowly so that everyone could understand.
questions.explanation: Different subject (everyone) + past → **so that everyone could understand her**.

pairs.right: in order to work in Seoul.
so that we wouldn't wake the baby.

questions.explanation: Purpose: *in order to, so that, so as not to*. *In case* expresses a precaution, not purpose.

questions.correction: so as not to be late
questions.explanation: Negative purpose → **so as not to / in order not to + verb**.

options: I went to the pharmacy for some medicine.
I went to the pharmacy for buy some medicine.
I went to the pharmacy for buying some medicine.
I went to the pharmacy so that buy some medicine.
questions.explanation: **for + noun** (*some medicine*) is correct. With a verb, we need *to buy*.

questions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: **so that + subject + could + verb**: *We left early so that we could find a parking space.*

lessons.title: Result: So...That, Such...That, Therefore
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan akibat dengan so...that, such...that, therefore, as a result, dan consequently.
objectives: Use so + adjective/adverb + that and such (a) + (adjective) + noun + that
Use therefore, as a result and consequently to link sentences
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### so ... that / such ... that
Both show a **cause** (something extreme) and its **result**.

| Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- |
| **so** + adjective/adverb + that | The exam was **so difficult that** most students failed. |
| **such** + a/an + (adjective) + singular noun + that | It was **such a difficult exam that** most students failed. |
| **such** + (adjective) + plural/uncountable noun + that | They were **such kind people that** we felt at home. / It was **such awful weather that** we stayed in. |
| **so** + many/few + plural noun + that | There were **so many people that** we couldn't see. |
| **so** + much/little + uncountable noun + that | I had **so little time that** I skipped lunch. |

Tip: **so** goes with adjectives/adverbs; **such** goes with nouns (with or without an adjective).

*That* is often omitted in informal speech: *I was so tired I fell asleep.*

### Sentence linkers of result
| Linker | Style | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| so | informal, joins clauses | It was late, **so** we went home. |
| therefore | formal | The factory closed. **Therefore**, many jobs were lost. |
| as a result | neutral | Prices rose. **As a result**, sales fell. |
| consequently | formal | It rained heavily. **Consequently**, the match was cancelled. |

*Therefore* can also go in the middle: *The factory closed, and many jobs were **therefore** lost.*

### as a result of / because of + noun
To give the cause as a noun: *The match was cancelled **as a result of** the rain.*

### Common errors
| ✗ Wrong | ✓ Right |
| --- | --- |
| such difficult | **so** difficult |
| so a nice day | **such** a nice day |
| It was a so good film. | It was **such a** good film. / The film was **so** good. |
| Therefore he left. (no comma, informal text) | **So** he left. / **Therefore**, he left. |

> **Catatan:** *so ... that* = *begitu ... sehingga* (dengan kata sifat); *such ... that* = *begitu ... sehingga* (dengan kata benda). *Therefore / As a result / Consequently* = *oleh karena itu / akibatnya* dan biasanya di awal kalimat baru dengan koma.

examples.en: It was such a hot day that we stayed indoors.
examples.id: Hari itu begitu panas sehingga kami tetap di dalam rumah.

examples.id: Kuliahnya begitu menarik sehingga tidak ada yang ingin kuliah itu berakhir.

examples.id: Pabrik itu tutup. Akibatnya, ratusan orang kehilangan pekerjaan.

vocabulary.example: Sales fell. Consequently, the shop closed.
The road is closed; therefore, we must take another route.
The match was cancelled as a result of the storm.
I had so little time that I skipped lunch.
Prices rose sharply. As a result, demand fell.

grammar.example: She ran so fast that nobody could catch her.
It was such a long journey that we slept on the bus.

grammar.pattern: Sentence. + Therefore / As a result / Consequently, + sentence.

mistakes.wrong: The exam was such difficult that most students failed.
mistakes.right: The exam was so difficult that most students failed.
mistakes.why: Use so before an adjective without a noun.

mistakes.wrong: It was so a nice day that we went to the beach.
mistakes.right: It was such a nice day that we went to the beach.
mistakes.why: Use such a before an adjective + singular noun.

mistakes.wrong: There were so much people that we left.
mistakes.right: There were so many people that we left.
mistakes.why: People is plural and countable, so use so many.

sections.summary: Use **so + adjective/adverb + that**, **such (a/an) + adjective + noun + that**, and **so many/much/few/little + noun + that** to show extreme causes and results. Link sentences with **so, therefore, as a result, consequently**. *Ringkasan: so + adjective; such + noun.*

reviewCards.front: so many / so much + noun + that
It was such a good film. / The film was so good.

questions.instructions: Hint: the gap is followed by a + adjective + noun.
questions.text: It was ___ a hot day that we stayed indoors.
questions.explanation: **such a + adjective + noun** (*such a hot day*). *So* goes directly before an adjective without *a*.

questions.sentence: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
answers: It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.
questions.explanation: *so + adjective* → **such a + adjective + noun**: *It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.*

questions.text: There were ___ many people at the concert that we couldn't see the stage.
answers: so
questions.explanation: **so many + plural noun + that**.

questions.prompt: Complete the text with words from the bank.
questions.text: The factory closed last year. ___, hundreds of people lost their jobs. It was ___ a shock that the whole town was silent for days. Unemployment rose ___ quickly that many families moved away.
answers: As a result
such
so
questions.explanation: **As a result** (result linker); **such a shock** (such + a + noun); **so quickly** (so + adverb).
Before an adjective without a noun, use **so**: *so difficult*.

questions.prompt: Rewrite as two sentences using consequently.
questions.sentence: It rained heavily, so the match was cancelled.
answers: It rained heavily. Consequently, the match was cancelled.
questions.explanation: **Consequently** (formal) starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

lessons.title: Writing a Balanced Argumentative Essay
lessons.summary: Menulis esai argumentatif yang seimbang dengan linker penambahan dan urutan serta kosakata isu sosial.
objectives: Use addition and sequencing linkers (furthermore, moreover, in addition to, firstly, finally)
Organise a balanced essay with on the one hand / on the other hand
Use vocabulary for social issues and debate
lessons.completionCriteria: Write the essay and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Tulis esai dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Structure of a balanced (for-and-against) essay
| Paragraph | Content | Useful language |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Introduction | Present the topic and why it is controversial | *Nowadays, ... It is often argued that...* |
| 2. Arguments for | 2–3 points with reasons/examples | *Firstly, ... Furthermore, ... For example, ...* |
| 3. Arguments against | 2–3 points with reasons/examples | *On the other hand, ... Moreover, ...* |
| 4. Conclusion | Summarise and give your opinion | *In conclusion, ... On balance, I believe that...* |

### Addition linkers
| Linker | Grammar | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Furthermore, / Moreover, | + sentence (formal) | **Moreover**, it reduces pollution. |
| In addition, | + sentence | **In addition**, it creates jobs. |
| What is more, | + sentence (less formal) | **What is more**, it's cheap. |
| In addition to / Besides | + noun or **-ing** | **In addition to providing** jobs, the factory brings investment. |

⚠️ *In addition to* and *besides* are followed by **-ing**, not the infinitive: ✗ *In addition to provide*.

### Sequencing linkers
*Firstly / First of all / To begin with* → *Secondly / Next* → *Finally / Lastly* → *In conclusion / To sum up / On balance*

### Presenting both sides
- *On the one hand, ... On the other hand, ...*
- *Supporters/Opponents of ... argue that...*
- *It is often claimed that... However, ...*

### Social-issue vocabulary
| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| poverty | being very poor |
| homelessness | not having a home |
| unemployment | not having a job |
| discrimination | unfair treatment of a group |
| welfare | government help for people in need |
| raise awareness (of) | make people know about a problem |
| tackle / address (an issue) | try to solve a problem |
| controversial | causing strong disagreement |

### Style tips
- Avoid *I think* in every sentence; use impersonal phrases: *It could be argued that...*
- Support each point with a reason or example.
- Use a variety of linkers from this unit (contrast, purpose, result, addition).

> **Catatan:** Esai argumentatif yang baik **seimbang**: sajikan argumen pro dan kontra sebelum memberikan pendapat di kesimpulan. Gunakan *Furthermore/Moreover* untuk menambah poin, *On the other hand* untuk sisi lain, dan *In conclusion* untuk menutup.

examples.en: On the one hand, social media helps people stay in touch; on the other hand, it can make young people feel isolated.
examples.id: Di satu sisi, media sosial membantu orang tetap terhubung; di sisi lain, media sosial dapat membuat anak muda merasa terisolasi.

examples.en: In addition to reducing traffic, free public transport would help people on low incomes.
examples.id: Selain mengurangi kemacetan, transportasi umum gratis akan membantu orang berpenghasilan rendah.

examples.en: Furthermore, the scheme would raise awareness of environmental issues.
examples.id: Lebih jauh lagi, program itu akan meningkatkan kesadaran tentang isu lingkungan.

examples.en: On balance, I believe the benefits outweigh the costs.
examples.id: Secara keseluruhan, saya percaya manfaatnya lebih besar daripada biayanya.

vocabulary.example: Education is one way to reduce poverty.
Youth unemployment has risen.
Laws should protect people from discrimination.
The city must tackle homelessness.
The new law is highly controversial.
The advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

grammar.pattern: In addition to / Besides + noun / -ing, + clause
On the one hand, + clause. On the other hand, + clause.
grammar.example: On the one hand, it's fast. On the other hand, it's expensive.

mistakes.wrong: In addition to provide jobs, the factory will bring investment.
mistakes.right: In addition to providing jobs, the factory will bring investment.
mistakes.why: In addition to is followed by -ing (to is a preposition).

mistakes.wrong: In the other hand, cars are convenient.
mistakes.right: On the other hand, cars are convenient.
mistakes.why: The fixed phrase is on the other hand.
Moreover adds a similar point; use however for contrast, and don't add but.

sections.summary: A balanced essay has an introduction, arguments for, arguments against and a conclusion. Use **firstly, furthermore, moreover, in addition (to + -ing), on the other hand, in conclusion, on balance**, and social-issue vocabulary such as **poverty, unemployment, discrimination, tackle, raise awareness**. *Ringkasan: seimbang dulu, baru beri pendapat di akhir.*

reviewCards.front: On the one hand ... On the other hand ...
reviewCards.back: Di satu sisi ... di sisi lain ...
lebih besar daripada (the benefits outweigh the costs)

questions.instructions: Hint: the second sentence adds another positive point.
questions.text: Public transport reduces traffic. ___, it is better for the environment.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds a similar point → **Furthermore**. *However* shows contrast; *Despite* needs a noun.

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in order to make one balanced sentence.
fragments: social media helps people stay in touch;
questions.explanation: *On the one hand* (first side) → *on the other hand* (second side), separated by a semicolon.

questions.prompt: "Public transport in cities should be free for everyone." Write a balanced essay (180–250 words) discussing the advantages and disadvantages, and give your own opinion in the conclusion.
questions.explanation: Use four paragraphs and a range of linkers: contrast (*however, although*), purpose (*so that, in order to*), result (*as a result, therefore*) and addition (*furthermore, in addition to + -ing*).

questions.explanation: These words are essential for essays and debates about society.

segments: will bring investment to the region.

questions.context: The new law is highly ___: some people strongly support it, while others are completely against it.
options: controversial
conventional
convenient
confidential
questions.explanation: **Controversial** = causing strong disagreement. *Conventional* = traditional; *convenient* = easy/useful; *confidential* = secret.

unitTestQuestions.context: ___ his lack of experience, he got the job.
options: Despite
Although
However
Even though
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The gap is followed by a noun phrase (*his lack of experience*) → **Despite**. *Although/Even though* need a clause.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using in order to.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: He wanted to improve his English, so he moved to Australia.
unitTestQuestions.cue: Begin with: He moved to Australia ...
answers: He moved to Australia in order to improve his English.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Purpose with the same subject → **in order to + verb**.

unitTestQuestions.text: It was ___ an interesting lecture that nobody wanted it to end.
answers: such

unitTestQuestions.explanation: *In spite of* cannot be followed by a clause (*it was expensive*). Use **Although** (or *In spite of being expensive*).

unitTestQuestions.source: Nisa belajar keras supaya bisa lulus ujian.
answers: Nisa studied hard so that she could pass the exam.
Nisa studied hard so she could pass the exam.
Nisa studied hard in order to pass the exam.
Nisa studied hard to pass the exam.
Nisa studied hard so as to pass the exam.
Nisa studies hard so that she can pass the exam.
Nisa studies hard so she can pass the exam.
Nisa studies hard in order to pass the exam.
Nisa studies hard to pass the exam.
Nisa is studying hard so that she can pass the exam.
Nisa is studying hard in order to pass the exam.
Nisa is studying hard to pass the exam.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Supaya bisa* = **so that + can/could** or **(in order) to + verb**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct linkers for this essay paragraph.
unitTestQuestions.text: Many people can't afford housing in the city. ___, wages have not risen for years. ___, the government should build more affordable homes.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The second sentence adds another problem → **Moreover**; the last sentence is a conclusion/result → **Therefore**.

unitTestQuestions.explanation: Knowing the function of each linker helps you organise an essay logically.
